Subject: Acme POC: Integration plan and next steps

Hi Jared & Liz,

Thanks again for the call earlier today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff: 

POC goals / success criteria
- Validate Redwood can achieve <100ms median per-token latency at expected concurrency (50 concurrent streams).
- Demonstrate streaming chat + tool-calling for Acme's knowledge-base agent (calls to your internal document search and ticketing APIs).
- Establish cost baseline (tokens per session) and a path to optimize via batching and KV caching.

Evaluation plan / timelines
- Week 0 (this week): finalise success criteria, sign simple POC SLA, and run onboarding (credentials + network).
- Week 1: Integration sprint — SDK + API routes wired, streaming responses enabled.
- Week 2: End-to-end demo with sample production traffic; collect latencies and token-cost metrics.
- Week 3: Iterate on configuration (batching, quantization suggestions) and finalize handoff.

Ownership
- Acme: Jared (technical lead) — provide API specs and sandbox credentials; Liz (procurement) — handle SOW/PO.
- Redwood: Marissa (engagement lead) — project coordination and success criteria; Vivek (solutions engineer) — technical onboarding and integration support; Rishi (platform) — performance tuning and metrics.

Immediate next steps (action items)
1) Jared: share sandbox API docs and temporary service account for tool-calls by EOD Thu (2026-09-03).
2) Marissa: send POC plan + simple SaaS POC SLA (attached) and schedule kickoff session.
3) Vivek & Rishi: prepare SDK snippets and a short integration checklist focused on streaming and tool-calling patterns.

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf, api-integration-checklist.xlsx

If that looks good I’ll schedule a 60-minute kickoff for Monday, Sep 6 (PT).

Thanks —
Marissa

Hey Jared — quick technical notes that should address the SDK/API questions and make the integration straightforward. I’ll prepare code snippets for the kickoff.

SDKs & streaming
- Official SDKs: we support Node (redwood@npm) and Python (pip). Both SDKs have a streaming chat client that yields tokens/partial events. We’ll send sample code, but basic pattern:
  - instantiate client with API key
  - open a streaming chat session (client.chat.stream) and listen for token events
  - on complete, SDK returns final response and function call payload if tool-calling occurred

API routes & tool-calling
- Single streaming endpoint: https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/stream (supports tool-calling). Tool-call events arrive as a structured JSON chunk inside stream; SDK exposes a `onToolCall` handler.
- Function/tool contract: we support synchronous HTTP callbacks (your service receives a POST) or we can handle tool calls via a short-lived signed URL if you prefer not to accept inbound calls.

Auth & networking
- API keys for hosted flow — easy. For tighter networking we support mTLS between your VPC and Redwood Dedicated endpoints; for a short trial you can open outbound to the hosted endpoint and use a temporary API key. No IP allowlist required for hosted POC.

Performance notes / instrumentation
- We recommend using streaming for lower tail latency and to enable early render. For concurrency=50 we’ll default to continuous batching disabled initially so you can measure raw stream times; we’ll enable batching if you want cost savings in week 2.
- Metrics: SDK emits per-token latency, request-id; we’ll provide a prometheus export or hosted traces to your dashboard.

Attachments & examples I’ll bring to kickoff
- Node streaming chat snippet (tool-calling example)
- Example server glue for ticketing:createTicket endpoint and verification handshake
- Integration checklist (api-integration-checklist.xlsx)

Let me know if you prefer synchronous callbacks vs signed-URL style for tool-calling.

Thanks,
Vivek
